featured_reviews.name: Abdul Rehman
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’ve ever dreamed of truly bonding with the waiting area of a car service center, Chaggan Mittha is your spiritual home. Forget those rushed, impersonal service places where you barely have time to finish a coffee — here, time moves in a gloriously leisurely fashion. Your car won’t just be fixed; it will be nurtured, meditated over, and perhaps even sung lullabies until it’s truly ready to return to you.

The quality of their work? Absolutely impeccable. They don’t just change your oil — they probably analyze each drop under a microscope to ensure it’s been replaced at the molecular level. I imagine the mechanics in the back wearing lab coats and magnifying goggles, speaking in hushed tones as they delicately tighten each bolt like it’s a priceless artifact. In fact, the repair might take so long because they are personally negotiating peace treaties between your brake pads and rotors. The result? A car that feels like it’s fresh off the assembly line… after a small eternity of tender care.

Now, about the staff — I cannot emphasize enough how polite, helpful, and genuinely lovely they are. They greet you with smiles so warm you almost forget you’ve been waiting long enough to have your mail forwarded to the service center. Need an update on your car? They’ll give you the friendliest, most reassuring “It’s almost ready” you’ve ever heard in your life. And you’ll believe them. Every. Single. Time. Their kindness is so genuine, you’ll actually feel guilty about wondering if your car still exists.

Some people might call the pace “slow,” but I prefer to think of it as “mechanically unhurried.” You can’t rush perfection, especially when it involves your safety on the road. This is not a drive-thru oil change joint; it’s a full-scale automotive spa. Your car leaves not just repaired, but rejuvenated. And you? You leave with your patience skills honed to saintly levels.

In conclusion, if you value craftsmanship, courtesy, and the unique opportunity to reflect deeply on your life choices while waiting for your car, Chaggan Mittha is unmatched. Come for the repairs, stay because — well, let’s be honest — you’ll have to. And when you finally drive away, you’ll swear the wait was almost worth it. Almost

featured_reviews.name: Preet Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I genuinely would not recommend buying an EV from this dealership. My experience after purchasing the vehicle was very disappointing. Until the delivery is completed, they speak very politely and behave professionally, but once the vehicle is sold, their attitude completely changes.

The after-sales service is extremely poor. If any issue arises in the vehicle, instead of supporting the customer, they immediately blame the customer and say it is “your mistake.” Even if a small internal part gets damaged or broken, they charge unrealistically high repair costs.

What disappointed me the most was the way customers are treated after the purchase. The owner seriously lacks professionalism and basic customer-handling skills. A customer expects support, respect, and proper service after spending their hard-earned money, but unfortunately that is not what you receive here.

I purchased the EV from this shop based on trust, but after my experience, I honestly cannot recommend anyone to buy an EV from here. Please think carefully before making a purchase.

The 4-star rating honestly looks completely fake. Customers spend thousands on these Maxim scooters, but within just a few months the scooters start giving problems or stop working altogether. The worst part is the after-sales support — even basic spare parts take months to arrive from Haryana, leaving customers helpless without their vehicle for weeks or even months.

The atmosphere at the dealership itself says a lot. Dealers are constantly seen arguing with frustrated customers instead of solving their issues professionally. Rather than providing support, they try to avoid responsibility, and in some cases even threaten customers with police complaints when people demand proper service for the money they paid.

The manufacturer may be responsible for the poor product quality, but the dealers are equally responsible for creating a false image and misleading customers into believing these products are reliable. Once the payment is done, the reality becomes completely different.

People work hard for their money and deserve proper service and respect, not excuses, delays, and arguments. Think twice before purchasing from them.
